Who is Nest Health?

As the first value-based care provider built for families, Nest is on a mission to make comprehensive medical, behavioral, and social care radically accessible to America’s highest risk families. Founded in 2022 by Former Secretary of Health of Louisiana and practicing OB-GYN, Dr. Rebekah Gee, and Rebecca Kavoussi, Nest is the first-of-its-kind family-based, in-home, and virtual care model; this includes primary adult and pediatric care, mental health and nutrition support, vaccinations and labs, same-and-next-day acute visits, chronic condition and transitions of care management, social services and navigation, and more. Nest’s innovative model has resulted in partnerships, unlocking care for thousands of families across our markets. Nest’s early success has led to national traction across states and payers, laying the groundwork for future expansion to families across the United States.

 

What does it mean to be a part of a startup?

Working at a healthcare startup can be a unique experience with a fast-paced, ever-changing environment that can involve varied workloads, quick changes, and high expectations. Taking a position at a Healthcare startup allows for the opportunity to be high impact in disrupting the US healthcare system. You will have the chance to be creative, solution oriented, and have your voice heard! You will need to be flexible, accountable, and self-sufficient, and you might take on multiple roles. Here are some things you can expect:

  • Role Breadth- Your role may be less defined than in other settings, with the need to wear multiple hats & juggle various responsibilities

  • Learning opportunities- you will have the opportunity, at times, to function outside of your standard position and learn about new roles & areas

  • Fast Paced- Startups often must move faster than traditional large companies. This means you may be asked to cope with or advise on quick changes regarding systems or processes

  • Autonomy- You will need to be highly autonomous, as there is less structure and learning and development than at large orgs. This requires you to be able to learn asynchronously, as well as raise your hand when help is needed, or gaps are identified

  • Collaboration- With so many opportunities to build processes and improve how we deliver care to our patients, we rely heavily on one-another to communicate changes effectively to ensure seamless support across functions. This often requires this individual to give and receive feedback frequently and communicate challenges or opportunities effectively.

Nest Healthcare is a multi-state, Medicaid-focused healthcare organization that cares for pediatric and adult patients. The Medical Coder ensures every encounter is coded accurately, completely and compliantly, so Nest is paid correctly and our quality and risk data reflect the patients we serve.

The coder reviews provider documentation assigns ICD-10-CM, CPT and HCPCS Level II codes, and works with providers and billing to resolve documentation gaps and denials across multiple state Medicaid programs and managed care plans.

Key responsibilities

Coding and charge capture

• Review provider documentation and assign accurate ICD-10-CM, CPT and HCPCS Level II codes and modifiers for outpatient locations, telehealth, behavioral health and procedural encounters.

• Code across the age spectrum: well-child and EPSDT visits, immunization administration, developmental screenings, adolescent care, adult chronic disease management and preventive services.

• Select E/M levels using current AMA guidelines.

• Capture HCC and risk-adjustment diagnoses to the highest specificity supported by documentation.

• Support quality programs (HEDIS and state quality measures) through accurate CPT II and diagnosis coding.

• Meet productivity and accuracy targets (e.g., 95% or higher accuracy on audit).

Medicaid and multi-state compliance

• Apply state-specific Medicaid coding, billing and EPSDT rules for each state Nest operates in, including managed care organization (MCO) policies.

• Apply NCCI edits, Medically Unlikely Edits (MUEs) and Medicaid-specific modifier rules.

• Track and apply quarterly code updates and payer policy changes; flag changes that affect workflows.

• Follow HIPAA, AMA, OIG and Nest compliance policies at all times.

Documentation quality and provider education

• Send clear, compliant queries to providers when documentation is incomplete, conflicting or unclear.

• Share recurring documentation gaps with leadership and help develop provider tip sheets and training.

Denials and revenue cycle support

• Review and correct coding-related claim edits, rejections and denials; support appeals with coding rationale.

• Partner with billing, credentialing and clinical operations to resolve root causes.

• Participate in internal and external coding audits and implement corrective actions.

Required qualifications

• Active coding credential from AAPC or AHIMA: CPC, COC or CCS.

• 5+ years of professional-fee medical coding experience.

• Working knowledge of ICD-10-CM, CPT, HCPCS Level II, E/M guidelines and NCCI edits.

• Experience coding for Medicaid and/or Medicaid managed care plans.

• Solid understanding of medical terminology, anatomy, physiology and pharmacology.

• Working knowledge of HIPAA and healthcare compliance requirements.

• High school diploma or equivalent; maintain required continuing education units (CEUs).

Preferred qualifications and skills

• Pediatric coding experience, including EPSDT, Vaccines for Children (VFC) and immunization administration coding.

• CRC (Certified Risk Adjustment Coder) or CPMA (Certified Professional Medical Auditor).

• Experience with Medicaid programs in more than one state.

• Behavioral health coding experience.

• Associate degree or higher in health information management or a related field.

• Experience with athenahealth EHR and claim scrubbers.

• Experience working with an AI-assisted or autonomous coding platform, including reviewing, validating and correcting AI-suggested codes.

• Strong attention to detail, independent judgment and the ability to explain coding decisions clearly to providers.

Work environment

• Primarily computer-based work; requires a secure, HIPAA-compliant workspaace if remote.

• Ability to sit for extended periods and use a computer and dual monitors for most of the workday

  • Great benefits and competitive compensation

Why choose Nest Health?

Nest and its leaders have won multiple awards including Rock Health's Next-Gen Pediatric innovations, New York Times Top Five Who Spread Hope, New Orleans City Business Power 50, and CB Insights Digital 150. Additionally, Nest has become a prominent thought and brand leader garnering national attention from outlets such as 60 Minutes, Business Insider, NYTimes, Fierce Healthcare, Axios , and others. More recently, they were recognized on Inc.'s Female Founder 500 List for 2025.

 

Learn more about us at https://www.nesthealth.com/.

To learn more about the Nest care model, watch this video, by the award- winning HBO Katrina Babies filmmaker Edward Buckles, JR.
